reviews.overall: Em đã chọn đúng đề, ghi đúng các số được dùng và chia thân bài theo hai giai đoạn hợp lý. Tuy nhiên, Overview chưa nêu rõ Thailand đạt đỉnh năm 2006 rồi giảm; cụm “slight fluctuations” làm sai mức biến động. Bài này em soát chưa kỹ: câu mở bài thiếu động từ bị động, còn nhiều câu ghép bằng dấu phẩy hoặc dùng sai dạng động từ. Cô yêu cầu em sửa các câu được đánh dấu và viết lại Overview để người đọc thấy đủ ba xu hướng chính.
reviews.dataGrouping: Em chia Detail 1 cho giai đoạn 2003–2006 và Detail 2 cho giai đoạn 2006–2009; cách chia này phù hợp vì 2006 là năm Thailand đạt đỉnh. Hai Detail đều có ít nhất hai câu và dùng số của cả ba nước. Em cần làm rõ Argentina vượt Australia năm 2006 và giới hạn nhận xét Thailand giống Australia vào riêng giai đoạn 2006–2009.

reviews.originalEssay:
The table illustrates how much cars made in three countries over a 6-year period commencing in 2003. 
   Overall, there was a general increase in car production in Argentina and Thailand, whereas the opposite trend was observed in the case of Australia. Despite slight fluctuations in Thailand, but it maintained the higher figures throughout the year.   
   To elaborate, in 2003, the output in Argentina and Thailand was 235,088 and 735,852, after that, it was significantly rose to 352,759 and 1,162,356 respectively in 2006. The figures in Australia witnessed the pronounced fall from 452,163 to 341,268 at the same time. 
   Regarding the final time, the production of car in Argentina continued to rise to 466,089 in 2009. By contrast, Australia's figures dropped to 245,624 in 2009. Additionally, Thailand's production followed the similar trend with Australia, it decreased to 999,963, however, the figures remained by far the highest in the period of time.

Regarding the final time, the production of car in Argentina continued to rise to 466,089 in 2009. By contrast, Australia's figures dropped to 245,624 in 2009. reviews.suggestedRevision:
The table compares how many cars were manufactured in Argentina, Australia and Thailand in 2003, 2006 and 2009.

Overall, car production rose steadily in Argentina and fell steadily in Australia. Thailand's output climbed to a peak in 2006 before declining in 2009, but it remained the highest of the three countries in every year. Argentina also overtook Australia by 2006.

In 2003, Thailand produced 735,852 cars, compared with 452,163 in Australia and 235,088 in Argentina. By 2006, Thailand's figure had surged to 1,162,356, while Argentina's had increased to 352,759. In contrast, Australian production had fallen to 341,268, leaving it slightly below Argentina's.

From 2006 to 2009, Argentina's output continued to rise, reaching 466,089 cars. Over the same period, Australia's figure dropped further to 245,624. Thailand's production declined from its 2006 peak to 999,963 cars in 2009. Despite this fall, Thailand still manufactured more than twice as many cars as Argentina in the final year.

reviews.suggestedRevision:
The two line charts compare the numbers of male and female prisoners in a European country between 1911 and 2001.

Overall, the male prison population was higher than the female population in every year shown. The number of men in prison fell early in the period but rose sharply towards the end, especially between 1971 and 1981. By contrast, the female count declined steeply to 1941, fluctuated afterwards and finished below its initial level.

In 1911 and 1921, there were about 18,000 male prisoners. This figure fell to roughly 10,000 in 1931, its lowest point, before returning to nearly 20,000 by 1951. It remained close to that level until 1971. A sharp increase then took it to approximately 39,000 in 1981, followed by a more gradual rise to around 46,000 in 2001.

The number of female prisoners started at about 3,200 in 1911 and dropped to a low of approximately 500 in 1941. It rose to roughly 1,500 by 1961, then fell back to about 700 in 1971. From there, the figure increased steadily to around 1,900 in 2001.

The given line graph illustrates the proportion of female members of parliament in five European countries from 2000 to 2012. 
  Overall, there was a general increase in the share of female parliament members in most countries. Notably, Germany consistently recorded high figures throughout the period, while the UK witnessed the most dramatic growth.  
To elaborate, in 2000, Germany recorded the highest figure at around 33%, and this number rose slightly to nearly 37% in 2012. The figures for Italy also witnessed a similar upward trend, growing from 26% in 2000 to reach the highest point of almost 39% at the end of the period. Meanwhile, France showed some fluctuation, starting at 25%, peaking at 37% in 2004, before dropping back to 32% in 2012. 
  Regarding categories with lower starting figures, the share of female parliament members in Belgium grew significantly from 17% in 2000 to 28% in 2004, after which it remained relatively stable until 2012. A much larger increase was seen in the figures for the UK, where the proportion started at only 3% in 2000 but increased sharply to catch up with Belgium at 28% in 2012.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given pie charts illustrate the main reasons why students chose a particular university in the UK over 10 years ,commencing 1997
Overall, there was a general increase in the share of students choosing a university because of suitable degree courses and proximity to parental home. Notably, suitable degree courses was the most popular reason in both years.   
To elaborate, in 1997, 35% of students chose a university because of suitable degree courses, and this number rose slightly to 37% in 2007. The figures for proximity to parental home also witnessed a significant upward trend, growing from 10% to 22% over the same period.   
Regarding other categories, the proportion of students choosing quality of teaching grew minimally from 15% to 18%. In contrast, the figure for quality of resources dropped slightly from 21% to 17%. Almost no variation was seen in the figures for good sports and social activities, except for a sharp fall from 19% in 1997 to only 6% in 2007.
